subject: Future Tech
title: The Trolley Problem Goes Real
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Trolley Problem Goes Real.

hook.text: A self-driving car faces a crash. Swerve left and hit a cyclist, or right and hit a wall? Who does the algorithm choose?

buildup.text: The trolley problem was a philosophy thought experiment.

discovery.text: MIT's Moral Machine surveyed 40 million decisions across 233 countries. Moral preferences vary wildly by culture.

twist.text: In practice, AVs rarely face binary choices. They brake early, slow down, and avoid the dilemma with better prediction.

climax.text: The real ethical question isn't crash decisions. It's whether delaying safe AVs to achieve perfection costs more lives.

punchline.text: The biggest ethical failure may be waiting too long.

quiz.question: What did MIT's Moral Machine study reveal?
options: All cultures agree on crash ethics
Moral preferences vary widely by culture
People prefer AVs to always protect passengers
